The near-exact 1.0037 ratio partly reflects a slightly stale Guinea figure rather than a truly tight match.

nyc_found: "In 2024, there were 2,192 unintentional drug poisoning (overdose) deaths in NYC compared with 3,056 deaths in 2023, a decrease of 864 deaths." (footnoted: "Data for 2023 and 2024 are provisional and subject to change")

NYC's number is also explicitly marked provisional and subject to revision.

nyc_found: Socrata dataset wq7q-htne, row sectors_sector="Total", category_full="Total": cy_2024_tco2e = 47,944,551.47 metric tons CO2e

Caveat worth noting: NYC's inventory is a consumption-based city GHG protocol (counts emissions from electricity generated elsewhere but used in the city) while Denmark's national total is a territorial/production-based inventory -- a standard but real accounting-boundary difference inherent to any city-vs-country emissions comparison.

nyc_found: "DSNY collects 24 million pounds of trash, recycling, and compostable material every day."
match_found: "Total weight: 10,100 tons" (Eiffel Tower key figures page)
conflict: NYC's own DSNY monthly tonnage data (a separate Open Data resource) suggests actual curbside refuse/recycling/organics collection runs closer to roughly 9,700-9,800 short tons (about 8,800-8,900 metric tonnes) per day on average in 2025 -- meaningfully below the 10,886-tonne figure derived from the marketing page, though the two sources may not cover identical waste streams (litter baskets, lot cleanups, etc.).
finding: The unit conversion from 24 million pounds to 10,886 tonnes is arithmetically correct (via 12,000 short tons), but the source figure is explicitly rounded to two significant figures ('24 million'), so presenting '10,886 tonnes' implies false precision. The claim's wording ('trash and recycling') also omits 'compostable material,' which the source's total explicitly includes.

nyc_found: "The New York metropolitan area is the most linguistically diverse urban center in the world... Based on a decade of work, ELA has mapped 700-plus language varieties (and counting) to over 1200 significant sites around the metropolitan area." (elalliance.org; the page never says "five boroughs")
match_found: "Indonesia: 710 languages" (Our World in Data, sourced from Ethnologue's count of living languages)
finding: The source explicitly attributes its 700-plus count to 'the New York metropolitan area,' not the City of New York -- a broader region including parts of New Jersey, Connecticut, and the Hudson Valley -- so calling it 'New York City' overstates the claim's geography. The two counts also measure different things: Indonesia's total is a linguistic census of that country's native/indigenous living languages, while ELA's tally is an informal, ongoing community-mapping count of immigrant and heritage languages, not languages indigenous to the region.

nyc_found: "Across the city, murder declined by 20.2% (305 vs. 382), with 77 fewer murders compared to 2024."

The word 'murders' does not appear anywhere in the Houston article. Without HPD's own murder-specific figure, it is not clear the two counts are built the same way, even though both are accurately quoted.

nyc_found: NYC Mayor's Management Report, DOC section: "The average daily population (ADP) in Fiscal 2025 was 6,823, an increase of nearly 10 percent from Fiscal 2024." (ADP trend: FY21 4,961, FY22 5,559, FY23 5,873, FY24 6,206, FY25 6,823 -- rising every year)

Given DOC's own steadily rising ADP trend (up nearly 10 percent in the latest year alone), NYC's true jail population as of early 2026 is plausibly already close to or above Switzerland's figure, not safely below it as the 1.0434 ratio implies.
